title: Dark Screens: The Pandemic and the Movies
description: In March 2020, COVID-19 shut down movie theaters across the entire planet. Amid postponements, drive-ins and the war over release windows, the way films are released would never be the same.

title: Social Media Shaping Cinema
description: TikTok, X, Instagram and Letterboxd wrested control of the conversation from the studios: memes created Barbenheimer, sank Morbius's comeback, revived forgotten songs and turned Gen Z into the stars of the multiplex.

title: The New Wave of Horror
description: After the pandemic, horror became the safest bet at the box office. From Smile and Barbarian to The Substance and Sinners, the genre broke out of its niche, won over the Oscars and spread around the world.

title: Internet Creators Hit the Big Screen
description: From the Philippou brothers to Kane Parsons, Curry Barker and Markiplier, filmmakers who came up on YouTube traded their channels for film sets and, in 2026, dominated the horror box office.

title: Hollywood on Strike and the Fight over AI
description: In 2023, writers and actors brought Hollywood to a halt for months to demand their share of streaming and protection against artificial intelligence. Soon after, AI took center stage for good.

title: The World Beyond Hollywood
description: After Parasite, films in languages other than English take over the Oscars and the box office, from Japan to India, from China to Korea. Until Brazil, at last, wins its first Academy Award with I'm Still Here.

title: The Streaming Wars and the Mergers
description: From the launch of Disney+ to the sale of Warner Bros.: how the race for subscribers ended in budget cuts, shelved films and the merger of two of Hollywood's oldest studios.

title: Superhero Fatigue and the Return of the Event Movie
description: After Endgame, the shared-universe formula wears thin, while Top Gun, Avatar, Dune and Nolan prove that audiences still want spectacle, as long as it feels one of a kind.
